land.text: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Uch Turpan, the Tarim Basin cities held by the Dughlat emir Mirza Abu Bakr, a vassal ruler under Moghulistan, until Sultan Said Khan took them in 1514

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Moghulistan row still contains these cells until 1518 and opens Eastern Moghulistan in 1519; the dossier starts in 1514, the year both pages give for Said Khan's conquest.

land.text: Altishahr (Tarim Basin) annexed by the Dzungar Khanate (Dzungar conquest of Altishahr infobox)

successors.note: 1680. Nominal Chagatayid khans reigned under Dzungar suzerainty until 1705 (Yarkent Khanate page); Cliopatria's Dzungar shape takes the cells in 1683 (2,069) and 1687 (1,211).

capitals.name: Yarkent (Yarkand)
capitals.note: Sultan Said Khan page: 'The capital of this state was Yarkand'; Yarkent Khanate page infobox: Capital Yarkent, and 'The previous Dughlat state ... also used Yarkent as the capital of state'. Said Khan first took Kashgar in May 1514.

correction.text: Kashgar (taken May 1514), Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Uch Turpan: 'other cities of Yarkand state - Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu, and Uch Turpan - joined him'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Eastern Moghulistan begins in 1519, but Said Khan took Kashgar in May 1514 and the Yarkent Khanate page dates the khanate to 1514 ('founded by Sultan Said Khan in 1514 after he took Kashgar, Yarkent and Hotan'). The 1519 outline is used for 1514-1518: 3,098 of its 3,289 cells lie in the gazetteer's Tarim Basin, and the page lists Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Uch Turpan as the cities that joined him. No infobox area on any page opened.

938,558 km2 for 1519-20: the Tarim Basin (3,098 of 3,289 cells in the gazetteer's Tarim Basin; Turfan-Hami is left out, 61 of 685 cells, which is right because Turpan and Hami were Mansur Khan's separate Turpan Khanate: Turpan page, 'Mansur conquered the kingdom ... in 1513'). None of the pages opened gives an area, so no infobox comparison.

938,660 km2 for 1521-46: the 1519 outline unchanged (+0.01%). Said Khan's raids of 1527-1532 on Bolor, Badakhshan, Ladakh and Kashmir (Yarkent page) are 'looting expeditions', not annexations, and the shape stays the Tarim Basin.

938,590 km2 for 1547-81: unchanged. The 1570 conquest of Turpan (Turpan page) is not in the Cliopatria shape; the ledger gain of 1570 adds it, so the renderer should apply the event on this shape from 1570.
938,151 km2 for 1582-87: unchanged (-0.05%); no dated change on the pages opened. Turpan stays added from 1570 by the ledger.
936,509 km2 for 1588-1608: unchanged (-0.2%, a few border cells); no dated change on the pages opened.

936,394 km2 for 1609-35: unchanged; the Yarkent Khanate page and the Moghulistan page ('subkhanates springing up with centers at Kashgar, Yarkand, Aksu and Khotan') describe the khans' loss of power to the khojas, not a loss of land.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin outline unchanged; holds 1636-1679, the Dzungar conquest of 1680 ends it

keyframe_review.note: 936,577 km2 for 1636-82: the same Tarim Basin outline, but its years should end in 1679. The Altishahr page has Galdan at Hami and Turpan by 1679 and in the Tarim Basin in 1680 ('The year 1680 seems to have been accepted by most authorities'; the range in the literature is 1678-1683) and its infobox gives 'Altishahr (Tarim Basin) annexed [by the] Dzungar Khanate'. The shape is unchanged; the ledger loss of 1680 ends it, and Turfan-Hami (added 1570) is lost at confidence 1 in 1678.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but not an independent state: the Tarim Basin under the Dzungar Khanate after 1680

keyframe_review.note: 340,765 km2 for 1683-86 (1,211 cells in the southern Tarim, 35.4-39.4 N): not Yarkent land any more. The Altishahr page's infobox: 'Altishahr (Tarim Basin) annexed [by the] Dzungar Khanate' (1678-1680), and Abdu'l Rashid II was made the Dzungars' vassal. Cliopatria's own Dzungar Khanate shape takes 2,069 of the 2,071 cells this row drops in 1683 and all 1,211 of these cells in 1687, so the khanate is shown ending 3 and 7 years after the page's 1680. The shape unchanged belongs to the dzungar-khanate dossier.

region.text: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Uch Turpan

ledger.note: 1514: Sultan Said Khan takes Kashgar and founds the Yarkent Khanate. 'In May 1514, Sultan Said Khan, grandson of Yunus Khan' ... took the city, dethroning Mirza Abu Bakr; 'other cities of Yarkand state - Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu, and Uch Turpan - joined him'; he 'ruled the Yarkent Khanate from September 1514 to July 1533'. The Moghulistan page: 'conquered the western Tarim Basin from Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat in 1514'. The page names the cities, not an outline: the Tarim Basin is my reading.

region.text: Turpan and its territories, with Hami, which had been Turfan's dependency since 1513

ledger.note: 1570: Yarkand takes Turpan. 'in 1570, the Turpan Khanate was invaded by an army led by Abduraim Sultan', 'the governor of Khotan in the Yarkand Khanate'; 'Turpan came under the control of the Yarkand Khanate.' The Turpan page also has the Yarkent branch 'conquer' most of Turpan's territories in 1570. Hami was a dependency of Turfan from 1513 (Moghulistan page), so Turfan-Hami is the region.

ledger.counterpart: Turfan Khanate (Chagatayid khans of Turpan after 1570; no dossier)
ledger.note: 1678: Turpan is no longer Yarkent's. The Altishahr page lists the belligerents of 1678-1680 as 'Dzungar Khanate Turfan Khanate Kumul Khanate: Yarkent Khanate', so Turpan and Hami fought on the Dzungar side; 'Galdan had moved to the cities of Hami and Turpan, capturing or sieging the cities by 1679'. No page opened dates Turpan's loss to Yarkand; 1678 is the start of the war on the infobox and is a bridging year. Reviewer (2026-10-19): counterpart changed from turpan-khanate, whose dossier ends with its dissolve into this state in 1570 and cannot carry a 1678 gain; the Altishahr page names a 'Turfan Khanate' among the Dzungar belligerents and calls Abdu'l Rashid II 'son of Baba Khan of Turfan', and the Turpan Khanate page has 'embassies sent from Turpan to Beijing in 1647 and 1657'.

region.text: the Tarim basin, advancing through Aksu

ledger.note: 1680: Galdan invades the Tarim Basin. 'Later the following year Galdan led 120,000 Dzungar cavalry into the Tarim basin, advancing through Aksu'; the page notes 'The year 1680 seems to have been accepted by most authorities, though Zlatkin, 1964, suggests 1679' and that the date is 'variously given, ranging from 1678 to 1683'.

1680: the Dzungars annex the Tarim Basin. Infobox: 'Altishahr (Tarim Basin) annexed [by the] Dzungar Khanate', result 'Dzungar victory'; Galdan advanced 'through Aksu and Khotan killing Ismail's family and establishing Abd ar-Rashid Khan II', whom he 'made his vassal'.
1680: the fighting ends in a Dzungar victory (infobox dates 1678-1680). Riots in Yarkand in 1682 drove Abdu'l Rashid II to Ili (page) but the land stayed Dzungar.

1680: the Yarkent Khanate loses its independence. The Yarkent Khanate page and the Moghulistan page carry the khanate to 1705 ('conquered by the Dzungar Khan, Tsewang Rabtan in 1705'; Altishahr footnote 1706) as a khanate whose khans were Dzungar vassals: the dossier ends at the annexation of 1680 and leaves the nominal khans to the dzungar-khanate dossier as a vassal tint.

wars.name: Said Khan's conquest of the Dughlat emirate of Kashgar
belligerents: Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat (emirate of Kashgar)

zones.text: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Uch Turpan

wars.outcome: Said Khan took Kashgar in May 1514, dethroned Mirza Abu Bakr, and the other cities of the Dughlat state joined him.

wars.name: Said Khan's raids on Bolor, Badakhshan, Ladakh and Kashmir
wars.outcome: Looting expeditions: 'a campaign in Bolor in 1527-1528, a raid into Badakhshan in 1529, and looting expeditions into Ladakh and Kashmir in 1532'; no land gained on the pages opened.
wars.note: Said Khan died in 1533 on the way back from Ladakh (Said Khan page); his death year is 1531 in a footnote of the Yarkent page.

wars.name: Yarkand conquest of Turpan
wars.outcome: Abduraim Sultan, governor of Khotan, invaded in 1570 and 'Turpan came under the control of the Yarkand Khanate'.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Altishahr
wars.outcome: Dzungar victory: the Tarim Basin was annexed by the Dzungar Khanate and Abdu'l Rashid II installed as Galdan's vassal.
wars.note: Dates vary in the literature from 1678 to 1683; 1680 is the most accepted year (page footnote). Galdan was at Hami and Turpan by 1679.

certainty.note: The Tarim Basin oases are fixed points but the frontiers on the Tian Shan, Kunlun and Pamir sides and the Turfan frontier are approximate; no page opened names a treaty or survey line for the Yarkent Khanate.

notes: Cliopatria's Eastern Moghulistan (1519-1686) is the Tarim Basin and is the Yarkent Khanate of the pages (founded by Sultan Said Khan in 1514, capital Yarkand); the Turpan Khanate page, by contrast, says the Turpan Khanate was 'also known as the Eastern Moghulistan'. The row is kept under the Cliopatria label with the display name 'Yarkent Khanate (Eastern Moghulistan)'; Turpan (1487-1570) is the turpan-khanate dossier. Not merged with the other rows of Q1191125: moghulistan (1463-1518), eastern-chagatai-khanate (1492-1511) and western-moghulistan (1519-1565 here) are different Moghul realms; the pieces tile (Tarim here, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan in western-moghulistan). Disagreements: end of the khanate 1680 (annexation, Altishahr page) against 1705 (Yarkent and Moghulistan pages, Altishahr footnote 1706) and 1686 (Cliopatria); Said Khan's death 1533 or 1531; Abdurashid's reign 1533-1565 (Moghulistan page) or 1533-1560 (Abdurashid Khan page, opened for western-moghulistan). Dzungar Khanate page (opened for western-moghulistan) has 'In 1678, the Dzungars intensified their advance into Tarim Basin and captured Yarkand' and 'soon in 1680, Galdan led 120,000 men into the Yarkent Khanate and conquered it'. Unsettled: the eastern frontier before 1570 (Aksu and Uch Turpan joined Said Khan in 1514, but Mansur held Aksu as his court in 1503 per the turpan-khanate dossier); who held Turpan between 1570 and 1678 (the Altishahr page has the Turfan Khanate beside the Dzungars in 1678; the Turpan page's infobox says 'Disestablished 1660?'); the nominal Yarkent khans under Dzungar suzerainty 1680-1705 (Abdu'l Rashid II to 1682, Akbash Khan 1696, Muhammad Mumin 1695-1705 on the Yarkent page) are a vassal matter for the dzungar-khanate dossier. Counterparts expected in other dossiers: dzungar-khanate gain 1680 (and the 1683 and 1687 shape steps), turpan-khanate (its dissolve into this state in 1570 is mirrored by the gain here; its loss in 1678 is a bridging guess), moghulistan loss 1514. Gazetteer: Turfan-Hami and Tarim Basin exist; nothing missing.
